paragraphs.text: Short Stirling R9329 of 149 Squadron left RAF Lakenheath at 2045 on 20 August 1942 to lay mines off the Gironde estuary near Bordeaux. It crashed in Gibhill Wood, near Cornwood on Dartmoor, at 0325 on 21 August 1942. All seven crew died. The navigator's log survived; its last entry, about ten minutes before the crash, read 03.15 completely lost.

The sources disagree on why it came down. Dartmoor Explorations reports that the RAF accident report found the aircraft probably damaged by ground defences over France and that it flew into rising ground and caught fire. IBCC says it is believed to have been hit by anti-aircraft fire over Plymouth on the return. Dartmoor Explorations also notes a suggestion of friendly fire over Plymouth from the brother of one crewman, with no conclusive evidence.

The pilot was Pilot Officer Geoffrey Ernest Robertson, aged 25, of the RAFVR. IBCC records him as a Pilot Officer; Dartmoor Explorations lists him as a Sergeant. The other six were all sergeants: Jenkins (22), Simpson (26), Harris (20), Nicholson (21, forward gunner), Clarke (25) and Bond (19), according to Dartmoor Explorations.

A granite pillar was set up at the crash site in 2011. Four local men, Gordon Fowell, Alan Graham, Peter Sandover and Ian Stone, began planning it in 2009. It was unveiled at a dedication service by David Nicholson, nephew of Sgt Lawrence Nicholson.

notes: IBCC pages for Jenkins, Simpson and Bond returned HTTP 429 and Nicholson's too (only a search summary seen), so only Robertson is fully identified; I did not try to work around the rate limit. Clarke and Harris have no IBCC/CWGC data yet. Burial places, service numbers, CWGC links and roles for six men are still to find. Dartmoor Explorations does not say who maintains the pillar; poppies are usually placed around it. IWM lists Delamore Estate as location, so landowner may be involved: unconfirmed. Dartmoor Explorations cites Wings over Dartmoor (Lewis 2016) and Dartmoor Air Crashes (Jones 2015) - not read. IBCC says crash 19 miles WSW of Torbay; IWM-derived record says 8 miles inland, unchecked. Memorial window at St George's Church, Methwold (IBCC) is a lead for further sources. Existing record narrative 'went off course... fired on near Plymouth' is unsourced beyond IBCC. Facebook source on our record not used.
